heading: EXT. GLASS ORCHARD ON THE EDGE OF THE WORLD - DAWN

units.text: EXT. GLASS ORCHARD ON THE EDGE OF THE WORLD - DAWN
Trees of blown glass stand in orderly rows, each leaf a thin pane of green, each fruit a drop of amber light.
A pale sun climbs the horizon and the whole orchard begins to sing, a thin high note like a wet finger on a goblet.
At the center of the orchard stands the last living gardener, OLD MARGUERITE THORNBURY-ANYANWU (80s, a patchwork cloak, gnarled fingers wrapped in silk).
She tends a single tree with a pair of silver shears.
A cart creaks down the row.
In it sits a young KNIGHT, SIR DESMOND ALDERWICK-OKAFOR (20s, dented armor, a bandaged shoulder) with a girl in a blue cloak beside him, LYRA FAIRCHILD (10s, a glass lantern in her lap).
The cart stops.
Marguerite does not turn.
You're early. The fruit isn't ripe.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: We didn't come for fruit.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: Everyone comes for fruit.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: We came for the key.
units.name: LYRA

units.text: Marguerite sets down her shears.
Slowly, she faces them.
She studies the girl, then the knight, then the girl again.
She has your grandmother's eyes.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: Whose?
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: Hers.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: Lyra climbs down from the cart.
The orchard hums.
A single glass leaf falls and shatters on the ground.
My mother said you would know.
units.name: LYRA

units.text: Your mother was a clever child. And a foolish one.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: Careful, gardener.
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: I am always careful, boy. That is why I am still alive.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: A shadow slides across the orchard.
The glass trees dim.
Everything falls quiet, even the song.
Down the far row, wading through a thicket of shards, comes a tall figure in a cloak of crows: THE COLLECTOR (ageless, face half hidden by a mask of white bone).
He walks without a sound, and every glass fruit turns toward him as he passes.
Marguerite. You said I was not welcome.
units.name: THE COLLECTOR

units.text: You are not.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: Yet here I am.
units.name: THE COLLECTOR

units.text: He lifts a hand.
The glass trees shiver.
Desmond draws his sword and steps between the girl and the stranger, but the Collector's fingers close, and the sword shatters in the knight's hand.
Desmond!
units.name: LYRA

units.text: Desmond staggers.
Lyra runs to him and drops the lantern.
It cracks open, and a thin bright flame spills out onto the grass.
Marguerite and the Collector both freeze.
Child, don't --
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: Careful, little one.
units.name: THE COLLECTOR

units.text: The flame climbs a glass tree.
The tree rings like a bell.
Every leaf catches light.
Marguerite and the Collector both stagger back as the orchard blazes with color.
They scatter.
Desmond hauls Lyra into the cart.
Marguerite throws her cloak over her head.
The Collector, for the first time, steps back.
What have you done?
units.name: THE COLLECTOR

units.text: Reminded it who it belongs to.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: The song swells, joyous now.
The Collector's bone mask cracks across the brow.
He turns and walks back the way he came, crows streaming from his cloak.
Silence.
The fire gutters out.
The trees stand untouched, brighter than before.
Is it over?
units.name: DESMOND

units.text: For today.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: Lyra picks up the empty lantern, examines it, and holds it out to Marguerite.
I'm sorry.
units.name: LYRA

units.text: Don't be. It was ready.
units.name: MARGUERITE

units.text: She takes the lantern, tucks it under her cloak, and picks up her shears.
